newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power higher with cold forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power higher with cold forecast.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Midwest were quoted mostly higher Tuesday with forecasts of below-normal temperatures through to at least Nov 28, power brokers and marketers said.
Despite a strong rally in natural gas physicals prices, sources said gas was not having a major impact on electricity values.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals were pegged in the $25.50-27.50 range from $23.00-25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Monday.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were said to be steady in the $11.50-12.50 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Wednesday delivery was pegged higher at $21.00-23.00 from $20.50-22.50 on Monday.
Power in northern MAIN was said to be selling at higher levels, comparable to next-day prices in the MAPP region.
MAIN off peak power was assessed steady near $11.00-13.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday delivery were assessed at $21.00-24.00 from $23.00-25.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $15.00-17.00 per MWh.
December peak ECAR was talked higher at $21.00-21.50 from $20.25-20.50 on Monday, the brokers and marketers said.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Wednesday were talked at $21.00-23.00 from $20.50-22.50 on Monday.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.
December SPP was assessed steady at $23.75-24.25, the brokers and marketers said.
